source.repro: The cut GraphGenomeView issues for a whole-cohort graph view, taken directly rather than through the browser: `node ~/src/jb2plugins/jbrowse-plugin-graphgenomeviewer/node_modules/@gmod/gbz-base/bin/query.js <hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.gbz.db> --haplotype-index <hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.haplotype-index.anchored.db> --sample GRCh38 --contig <C> --interval <A..B> --context 1000 --snarls --haplotypes all --limit 100000 --resolve --format gfa --stats`, against the hosted HPRC database `https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/human-pangenomics/pangenomes/freeze/release2/minigraph-cactus/v2.1/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.gbz.db` and the haplotype index `https://jbrowse.org/demos/hprc/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.haplotype-index.anchored.db`. The six windows, as `--contig <C> --interval <A..B>`: ABCA7 chr19 1049407..1050096, C4 chr6 31972057..32055418, CFHR3/CFHR1 chr1 196753088..196837771, amylase chr1 103611080..103732636, 1q21.1 chr1 144419292..144572458 (re-taken at `--limit 100000` with the same node count, so its row stands), CFH demo window chr1 196640000..196900000. Those flags are the adapter's config defaults (`context` 1000, `subgraphSnarls` 'contained', `nodeLimit` 100000 — the rows below were taken at 50000, which no row approaches) plus the `haplotypes: 'all'` and `names: 'resolved'` GbzBaseSyntenyAdapter.getSubgraph passes when the session names no haplotype subset. Run it through the plugin's own node_modules, NOT `npx -p @gmod/gbz-base`, which costs ~37 s per invocation before the query starts. 'net' is the db plus haplotype-index range-read total the reader's own --stats reports; 'GFA' is the string the worker hands the main thread. The split and complete-bar columns apply walkRows' flank rule (a walk is complete when it reaches a reference node on both sides of the region) to the W lines; that script is not committed and the numbers reproduce from the command above.
source.notes:
CAN A WHOLE-COHORT GRAPH CUT CARRY WALK ROWS AT A REAL LOCUS. The picture walk rows draws — every haplotype as a bar on its own bp, so a private repeat copy has width the reference axis cannot give it — had only ever been cut at ABCA7, a 689 bp window.

It survives at C4, CFHR and the 260 kb CFH demo window, where the cut returns one walk per haplotype in 5-14 s. It does not survive at amylase or the 1q21.1 inversion, where 296 and 342 walks are split.

The gate is not window size: 260 kb works and 122 kb fails. It is also not snarl containment, which is what this record first claimed. What decides it is how the route builds its node set. Asking for the cohort grows a bp-radius neighbourhood around the reference walk and closes it over snarls, then reads walks out of that set, so a GBWT position whose successor left the set ends a walk and the remainder returns as another fragment. Naming the haplotypes takes the anchored route instead, whose node set is exactly the steps those walks make, with a run the reference does not carry kept however long it runs. An expansion of 188 kb therefore leaves a `context 1000` envelope and comes back in pieces on the one route, and is admitted whole on the other. `--snarls` reaches only the first route; the anchored one ignores it.

Naming them does not rescue everything. 1q21.1 with four named samples runs at 12,065 nodes and still returns 8 of 9 haplotypes in two pieces, so that locus is out of reach for its walk structure and not for any ceiling — its cohort cut here is 17,933 nodes against an adapter default of 100000. The walk leaves the window through the segmental duplication and returns, which no route repairs.

The slowest cut of the six is the 689 bp window the tutorial already ships. ABCA7's 56 s is haplotype identification rather than size: 452 of 463 chains hold no sampled GBWT position inside the cut, so naming them walks 898k steps.

Walk rows already computes `complete` per row and sorts the incomplete ones to the bottom without saying so, which is what makes amylase read as a short-bar distribution rather than as a cut that could not hold 296 of the walks.
